cloak, mantle
cloak, mantle. It is a poetic word, except that Herodotus also used it in two places.
Herodian, On Peculiar Words p. 36, 19: "The tragedians, however, both lengthen and shorten the alpha of the word in question (φᾶρος [cloak]), as in Aeschylus in the Women of Salamis."

this cloak bears witness for me

if only I had a cloak equal to the sky

Phasis (river of Colchis)
Phasis, a river of Colchis, which was believed to be the boundary between Asia and Europe: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 670.

coffered ceiling panel
coffered ceiling
Pollux 7, 122: "And ekphatnoma [coffered panel] (Hermann rightly reads phatnoma [coffered panel]) and kyma [wave molding] are parts of works in Aeschylus' Chamber-Makers (fr. 72)."

Hermann: "Hesychius: phatnōmata [coffered panels] -- plank-work. Photius: kalymmatia [small coverings] -- which some call phatnōmata [coffered panels]. So Aristophanes (fr. 54: 'how well he roofed the house with small coverings'). For kalymmation [small covering] is the vaulted part in coffered ceilings, which are phatnōmata [coffered panels]: which part is called Lesbian cymatium by Vitruvius 4, 6, 2, as it was called by Aeschylus, because it is curved with a sinuous bend."
but let one man finish a Lesbian wave in triangular rhythms on the coffered panel (thus Kuehn for emperainetō)
and ekphatnoma [coffered panel]
